implementation_notes: The library realization: every independent check produces a Validation<Seq<E>, T>, and Validation.combine(...).ap(constructor) applies the combining constructor while aggregating every invalid result. Choose it when the response must carry all validation messages; the trade-off is a dependency on Vavr and the loss of monadic composition inside the validated region.
pitfalls: No flatMap: sequential dependencies cannot be expressed without dropping out of Validation.
Validation.combine only accepts a constructor for the combined type, so post-processing the combined value happens after the fact, never inside the failure-accumulating region.

variants.name: CompletableFuture.thenCombine / allOf (concurrent, fail-fast)
variants.implementation_notes: The JDK realization: independent asynchronous effects are started as CompletableFuture stages and combined with thenCombine (pairwise) or allOf plus manual joining. allOf completes only after every supplied stage completes; if any stage fails, the aggregate completes exceptionally and successful values still need to be collected from the individual stages. It combines concurrent IO without a library, but it is fail-fast in its result shape rather than an accumulating validator.
pitfalls: thenCombine's BiFunction runs on the completing thread - blocking work there stalls the common ForkJoinPool; use thenCombineAsync for blocking code.
allOf returns CompletableFuture<Void> and waits for every input; if any fails, joining the aggregate throws and individual successful values still need manual collection.
There is no error accumulation: use a Validation library, or collect failures inside each stage as values.
